1: # STAMP
2: 
3: ## Executive summary
4: 
5: Stamp is a peel-and-press spread for toast. Each stamp is a 10 g disc on release film, in a printed card. Peel it off, press it onto hot toast, and the heat softens it into a layer. No knife, and no open jar. An unopened sheet is made for 12 months in a pantry. Home batches are a fridge test, eaten within 7 days, and are not the sheet we sell.
6: 
7: The buyer eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion, not a jar to carry or a knife to wash.
8: 
9: Cleaned New Zealand sales put spreads at about $275 million NZD in 2022 and about $341 million NZD in 2025, about 24% growth. Premium grew faster than value, from about $88 million NZD to about $113 million, against value at about $36 million to about $39 million.
10: 
11: A jar is a shared tub. A stamp is one portion. The sheet is $5.00 NZD for 80 g, or $6.25 NZD per 100 g, above the cleaned file's 90th percentile of $5.19. None of the 154 spread names is a portion or a peel-and-press product. The opening is the format.
12: 
13: ## Product
14: 
15: Four flavours launch together: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, and Peanut. A single-flavour sheet holds eight stamps. A mixed sheet holds two of each. Every sheet is 80 g and $5.00 NZD, so $6.25 NZD per 100 g.
16: 
17: Salted Butter is a shelf-stable butter spread, not a pat of fridge butter. The sheet prints the flavour name and then the word spread, because butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard in Australia and New Zealand. The sold disc is cultured butterfat and salt, 2 g of salt to 78 g of fat, with no added oil. It contains milk. The home batch is that salt ratio beaten into softened butter, chilled, and eaten within 7 days.
18: 
19: Raspberry is raspberries, caster sugar, and lemon juice cooked down. The home batch reduces 120 g of fruit, 30 g of sugar, and 5 g of lemon juice to 80 g. The sold disc is that paste at 10 g. The label says 150 g of raspberries per 100 g because of the reduction.
20: 
21: Yeast extract is our paste. It is not Marmite and it is not Vegemite, and those names are not on the pack. The home batch is yeast extract, tomato paste, black treacle, and salt. The sold formula is yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, and vegetable concentrate 2%. It contains gluten from barley.
22: 
23: Peanut contains peanuts. The home paste is roasted peanuts and salt, ground and portioned before the oil separates. The sold disc is roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% so the oil does not separate over 12 months, and salt 1.7%.
24: 
25: Every sheet, including Raspberry, is made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. The mixed sheet contains milk, gluten, and peanuts. Nutrition figures on the backs are calculated from these proportions and from published composition tables. They are not a laboratory assay, and this plan does not present them as tested. No certification mark is used.
26: 
27: Making is the same shape for each flavour. Deposit 10 g, give or take 0.5 g, onto release film, cut the disc, nest eight in the card, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check, or a film that will not release, is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. To use one, keep the sheet in a pantry, peel a stamp, press it onto hot toast, and wait a few seconds.
28: 
29: ## Market
30: 
31: These figures come from the cleaned sales file, not the raw spreadsheet totals. Money is in million NZD. The source column was stored in thousands of NZD and has been scaled so the unit is written out.
32: 
33: Spreads revenue was about $275 million NZD in 2022, about $305 million in 2023, about $319 million in 2024, and about $341 million in 2025. From 2022 to 2025 that is about 24% growth. The 2024 total sits a little above the raw column because blank revenue cells in that year were filled.
34: 
35: Value spreads moved from about $36 million NZD to about $39 million. Premium moved from about $88 million to about $113 million. Standard, still the largest tier, moved from about $151 million to about $189 million. Premium's rate of growth was faster than value's. Standard added the most dollars. A sheet priced like a value jar would be aimed at the slow part of the category. Stamp is priced above ordinary jars, toward a tier that grew, and away from where most of the money still sits.

The price is the portion film and the card. It is not a claim that the paste is a luxury version of the median jar.

102: ## Operations
103: 
104: Griffiths & Co, at 10 Cornwall Road, Waiuku, Auckland 2681, is the named manufacturer. The contact page prints 09 235 5435 and no email. Enquiries use the form. https://www.griffithsfoods.co.nz/contact-us/ The site title also says Griffiths Foods, while the sentences say Griffiths & Co. This is not a contract.
105: 
106: Services cover sauces, salad dressings, and dips: sachets from 5 g to 1.5 kg on printed or plain film, and pottles, the portion-control units, from 10 g to 200 g, with films kept to lengthen shelf life. https://www.griffithsfoods.co.nz/services A 10 g paste fits both ranges. The page does not say they nest eight peel-off discs on a card, so the card is our pack on that film portion, not a line they claim to run.
107: 
108: Neither page states a price. The $1.50 NZD sheet cost stays an assumption, not a Griffiths quote.
109: 
110: The drawn path is order in, deposit onto film, cut, nest eight, then a check for 10 g plus or minus 0.5 g and for release. Pass is packed and dispatched. Fail is rejected and does not ship.
111: 
112: Peanut paste and yeast extract thicken or slacken in the hopper, so deposit weight drifts. Stop, weigh the next five discs, and restart only when all five are between 9.5 g and 10.5 g. Failed discs are not nested. A release roll shows a fault only after spread is on it. Peel-test eight discs at the start of each roll. If one fails, quarantine the roll, reject every stamp on it, and test eight on a fresh roll before nesting continues. Nothing from that roll is packed or dispatched.
113: 
114: The diagram is that gate. Pass reaches dispatch, and a failed check stops.
115: :::figure
116: src: diagrams/process.png
117: max-height: 580
118: caption: Pass reaches pack and dispatch. A stamp that fails weight or release is rejected and does not ship.
119: :::
120: 
121: ## Information
122: 
123: Five rates use Customer, Order, Order line, Sheet, Product, Batch, Manufacturer, and Campaign. A single-flavour sheet is one product and eight stamps. A mixed sheet is two of each product. A batch deposits one product and supplies a sheet only if the check passed.
124: 
125: Repeat purchase rate divides customers with two or more orders by customers with at least one. Stamps per order divides the sum of sheet quantity times stamps on the sheet by the number of orders. Every sheet carries 8, including mixed. On-time dispatch divides orders sent on or before the promised date by orders that have a dispatch date. An order with no date is left out. Batch rejection rate divides weight rejects plus release rejects by stamps checked. Weight is outside 10 g plus or minus 0.5 g. Release means the film will not peel. Each stamp counts once, under the first failure, and rejects are not packed. Gross margin per sheet is an assumption, not a Griffiths quote and not a manufacturer field. A $5.00 NZD shelf price less 35% ($1.75) is $3.25, and less the assumed $1.50 is $1.75 NZD.
126: 
127: Two questions follow. Which flavour is reordered runs from customer to order to order line to sheet to product. A later single-flavour sheet counts. A mixed sheet does not. Which batch failed release is a release-reject count above zero. Those stamps supply no sheet. The manufacturer record says who ran the batch.
128: 
129: A medical effect cannot be answered. Nothing stores a symptom, a diagnosis, a test, or a health outcome, and the product claims none.
130: 
131: A reorder traces to a flavour. A failed release stays on the batch.

133: src: diagrams/erd.png

136: :::

The first paid work is assumed to be a trial batch for weight and film release, not a sales order. The first public step is assumed to be the Instagram video and one podcast request.
143: 
144: These 90 days ask whether the disc releases, whether the sheet survives a bag, and whether the gesture is clear on a phone. They are not a health claim or a tested nutrition panel.

138:     """Return sections of prose, figure, and row blocks."""
139:     sections: list[dict] = []
140:     current: dict | None = None
141:     prose: list[str] = []
142:     lines = text.splitlines()
143:     index = 0
144: 
145:     def flush() -> None:
146:         nonlocal prose
147:         if current is None:
148:             prose = []
149:             return
150:         chunk = "\n".join(prose).strip()
151:         prose = []
152:         if chunk:
153:             current["blocks"].append(("prose", chunk))
154: 
155:     while index < len(lines):
156:         line = lines[index]
157:         stripped = line.strip()

3: Locked from your choices in Stage 1. One number is a planning assumption and is marked as such: the manufactured cost that sits under the $5.00 shelf price.

5: ## What a Stamp is
6: 
7: A Stamp is a 10 g disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. You peel one off and press it onto hot toast. The heat softens it into a layer. No knife and no open jar.
8: 
9: An unopened sheet lives in a pantry for 12 months. The home recipes below are kitchen prototypes, eaten from the fridge within 7 days. Only the industrial formulas are the products we sell, and only those claim the 12-month date.
10: 
11: ## Who it is for
12: 
13: Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion of flavour without carrying a jar or washing a knife.
14: 
15: ## Range and price
16: 
17: | Sheet | Contents | Net weight | Shelf price | Price per 100 g |
18: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
19: | Salted Butter | 8 butter stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
20: | Raspberry | 8 raspberry stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
21: | Yeast extract | 8 yeast-extract stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
22: | Peanut | 8 peanut stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
23: | Mixed | 2 of each flavour | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
24: 
25: $6.25 per 100 g sits above about 90% of branded spread SKUs in the cleaned dataset (90th percentile $5.19 per 100 g). The median branded spread is $2.15 per 100 g. Fix & Fogg's SKUs sit around $2.65 per 100 g. The gap is the portion film and the card, which a jar does not have. The marker is on `data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png`.
26: 
27: ## How to use it
28: 
29: 1. Keep the sheet in a pantry.
30: 2. Peel one stamp off the release film.
31: 3. Press it onto hot toast.
32: 4. Wait a few seconds. The residual heat lays the spread across the slice.
33: 
34: ## Claims we will make
35: 
36: - Peel and press onto hot toast.
37: - One stamp is one portion, 10 g.
38: - Four flavours, sold as single-flavour sheets and a mixed sheet.
39: - No knife and no jar.
40: - Unopened sheet, 12 months in a pantry.
41: 
42: ## Claims we will not make
43: 
44: - Health treatment, "better for you," low-sugar, organic, or gluten-free.
45: - That Salted Butter is a pat of fridge butter. The sold disc is a shelf-stable butter spread. In Australia and New Zealand the word butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard (milkfat, no added oil). The sheet shows the flavour name, then the word spread. The ingredient list names cultured butterfat.
46: - That Yeast extract is Marmite or Vegemite. Those names, jars, and trade dress do not appear on the pack or the site.
47: 
48: ## Allergens
49: 
50: | Flavour | Contains | Also stated on every sheet |
51: | --- | --- | --- |
52: | Salted Butter | Milk | Made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. |
53: | Raspberry | No major allergen in the recipe | Same facility statement. |
54: | Yeast extract | Gluten (barley) | Same facility statement. |
55: | Peanut | Peanuts | Same facility statement. |
56: | Mixed | Milk, gluten, peanuts | Same facility statement. |
57: 
58: ## Home prototypes
59: 
60: Each batch is eight stamps, 80 g. Shape into 10 g discs, press each onto a square of baking paper, and chill until they hold. Eat within 7 days. These batches test flavour and the peel-and-press gesture. They are not the shelf-stable product.
61: 
62: **Salted Butter.** 78 g unsalted butter, softened, beaten with 2 g fine salt.
63: 
64: **Raspberry.** 120 g raspberries, 30 g caster sugar, and 5 g lemon juice, cooked and stirred until 80 g of thick paste remains. Cool before portioning.
65: 
66: **Yeast extract.** 55 g yeast extract, 15 g tomato paste, 8 g black treacle, and 2 g salt, warmed and stirred into a paste that holds a disc. This prototypes the salty yeast flavour. The sold paste is the industrial formula below, not a scooped jar of an existing brand.
67: 
68: **Peanut.** 85 g roasted peanuts and 1.5 g fine salt, ground to a firm paste and portioned before the oil separates.
69: 
70: ## Industrial formulas
71: 
72: Deposit 10 g ± 0.5 g onto release film, cut, nest eight discs in a card sheet, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check or a film that will not release is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. Shelf life is 12 months, ambient, unopened.
73: 
74: **Salted Butter.** Cultured butterfat and salt at the same 2 g salt per 78 g fat as the home batch. Moisture is low enough that the sealed disc stays stable in a pantry and still softens on hot toast. No added oil, so the dairy description stays honest. On the sheet the flavour name is Salted Butter and the word under it is spread.
75: 
76: **Raspberry.** The home ratio (raspberry, sugar, lemon), cooked to the same thick paste and deposited at 10 g. Stability comes from the solids in the cook and the seal, not from a preservative claim. The label says it is made with 150 g of raspberries per 100 g, which is this cook: 120 g of fruit reduced to 80 g.
77: 
78: **Yeast extract.** Our yeast-extract paste, deposited at 10 g: yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, vegetable concentrate 2%. The salt share matches the home batch. Barley malt extract sits above salt, and vegetable concentrate sits below it, so the ingredient list stays in the order above. Contains gluten. The flavour name is Yeast extract. The pack does not say Marmite or Vegemite.
79: 
80: **Peanut.** Roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% as the hard-fat stabiliser, and salt 1.7%, close to the 1.5 g salt in the home batch. The stabiliser keeps the disc from oiling off across 12 months. Contains peanuts.
81: 
82: The nutrition panels on the backs are calculated from these proportions and published composition figures. They are not a laboratory assay.
83: 
84: ## Manufactured cost (assumption)
85: 
86: You chose the $5.00 shelf price. You did not choose a cost target. Until Stage 4 prices a real manufacturer, the spec uses this stack:

90: | Shelf price | $5.00 | $0.63 |
91: | Retailer keeps 35% | $1.75 | $0.22 |

export const FALLBACK_RESPONSE: BotResponse = {
	topicId: 'unknown',
	topicTitle: 'Support Guide',
	answer:
		"I'm here to help with all questions about Stamp! You can ask about:\n\n• What Stamp is and how the peel-and-press system works\n• How to use it on hot toast\n• Our four launch flavours (Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, Peanut)\n• Allergens, nutrition, and ingredient disclosures\n• Pricing ($5.00 NZD per 8-stamp sheet / $6.25 per 100 g)\n• Where to buy and availability\n• Replacements for damaged or crushed sheets\n• How Stamp compares to supermarket jars\n\nWhat would you like to know?"
};

export function matchQuestion(input: string): BotResponse {
	const text = input.trim();
	if (!text) {
		return FALLBACK_RESPONSE;
	}

	const lower = text.toLowerCase();

	// 1. Check high-priority refusals and specific triggers first
	// Medical advice
	if (
		/\b(stomach|tummy|gut|digest|digestive|health|healthy|medical|medicine|cure|treat|remedy|sick|illness|disease|nausea|doctor)\b/i.test(
			lower
		)
	) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'medical_advice')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer, isRefusal: true };
	}

	// Claim bans (gluten-free, organic, low sugar, etc.)
	if (
		/\b(gluten[-\s]?free|celiac|coeliac|organic|low[-\s]?sugar|sugar[-\s]?free|better for you|diet)\b/i.test(
			lower
		)
	) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'claim_bans')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer, isRefusal: true };
	}

	// Crushed / damaged
	if (/\b(crushed|damaged|broken|squashed|ruined|torn|melted|complaint)\b/i.test(lower)) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'crushed_sheet')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
	}

	// Jar comparison
	if (
		/\b(jar|jars|versus|vs|fix & fogg|pics|nutella)\b/i.test(lower) &&
		/\b(compare|comparison|versus|vs|than|why|expensive|different|difference)\b/i.test(lower)
	) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'jar_comparison')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
	}

	// Nut / peanut / allergen
	if (
		/\b(peanuts?|nuts?|allergen|allergens|allergy|allergic|dairy|milk|lactose)\b/i.test(lower) &&
		!/flavour|flavor|range|varieties/i.test(lower)
	) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'allergens_peanut')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
	}

	// How to use
	if (
		/how (do i|to|can i) (use|apply|put|eat)/i.test(lower) ||
		/\b(instructions|directions|how does it work)\b/i.test(lower) ||
		(lower.includes('how') && lower.includes('use'))
	) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'how_to_use')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
	}

	// Price / cost
	if (
		/\b(price|pricing|cost|costs|expensive|nzd|\$|dollars?|cents?)\b/i.test(lower) ||
		/how much/i.test(lower)
	) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'price')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
	}

	// Where to buy
	if (
		/where (can i|to|do i) (buy|get|purchase|find|order)/i.test(lower) ||
		/\b(supermarket|supermarkets|stockist|stockists|stores?|shops?|retailers?|where to buy)\b/i.test(
			lower
		) ||
		(lower.includes('where') && (lower.includes('buy') || lower.includes('purchase')))
	) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'where_to_buy')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
	}

	// Flavours
	if (
		/\b(flavours?|flavors?|varieties|tastes?)\b/i.test(lower) ||
		(/what/i.test(lower) && /flavour|flavor/i.test(lower))
	) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'flavours')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
	}

	// What is a Stamp
	if (
		/what (is|are) (a )?stamp/i.test(lower) ||
		/tell me (about )?stamp/i.test(lower) ||
		/what('s| is) this/i.test(lower) ||
		(lower.includes('what') && lower.includes('stamp'))
	) {
		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'what_is_stamp')!;
		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
	}

	// Scoring fallback across remaining topics
	let bestTopic: Topic | null = null;
	let bestScore = 0;

	for (const topic of TOPICS) {
		let score = 0;
		for (const pat of topic.patterns) {
			if (pat.test(lower)) score += 3;
		}
		for (const kw of topic.keywords) {
			if (lower.includes(kw.toLowerCase())) score += 1;
		}
		if (score > bestScore) {
			bestScore = score;
			bestTopic = topic;
		}
	}

	if (bestTopic && bestScore >= 2) {
		return {
			topicId: bestTopic.id,
			topicTitle: bestTopic.title,
			answer: bestTopic.answer,
			isRefusal: bestTopic.isRefusal
		};
	}

	return FALLBACK_RESPONSE;
}

<script lang="ts">
	import { matchQuestion, TOPICS, type BotResponse } from '$lib/knowledge';

	interface Message {
		id: number;
		sender: 'user' | 'bot';
		text: string;
		topicTitle?: string;
		isRefusal?: boolean;
		timestamp: string;
	}

	let userInput = $state('');
	let messages: Message[] = $state([
		{
			id: 1,
			sender: 'bot',
			text: "Kia ora! I am Stamp's automated support assistant. Ask me anything about our peel-and-press toast spreads, flavours, allergens, pricing, or application instructions.",
			timestamp: 'Just now'
		}
	]);

	let isThinking = $state(false);

	const quickQuestions = [
		'What is a Stamp?',
		'How do I use it?',
		'What flavours are there?',
		'Does the Peanut stamp contain nuts?',
		'Is it gluten-free?',
		'How much is a sheet?',
		'Where can I buy it?',
		'My sheet arrived crushed.',
		'Will this help my stomach?',
		'How does it compare with a jar of peanut butter?'
	];

	function getTimeString() {
		const now = new Date();
		return now.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
	}

	function handleSend(textToSend?: string) {
		const query = (textToSend || userInput).trim();
		if (!query) return;

		// Add user message
		const userMsg: Message = {
			id: Date.now(),
			sender: 'user',
			text: query,
			timestamp: getTimeString()
		};
		messages.push(userMsg);
		userInput = '';
		isThinking = true;

		// Slight delay for realistic chat feel
		setTimeout(() => {
			const result: BotResponse = matchQuestion(query);
			const botMsg: Message = {
				id: Date.now() + 1,
				sender: 'bot',
				text: result.answer,
				topicTitle: result.topicTitle,
				isRefusal: result.isRefusal,
				timestamp: getTimeString()
			};
			messages.push(botMsg);
			isThinking = false;
		}, 180);
	}

	function handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
		if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) {
			e.preventDefault();
			handleSend();
		}
	}
</script>

<svelte:head>
	<title>Customer Support Chatbot — STAMP</title>
	<meta
		name="description"
		content="Interactive customer support assistant for Stamp toast spreads. Get instant answers on ingredients, allergens, pricing, and how to apply Stamp."
	/>
</svelte:head>

<div class="chat-page">
	<div class="chat-container">
		<header class="chat-header">
			<div class="header-status">
				<div class="avatar">STAMP</div>
				<div>
					<h1 class="chat-title">Stamp Customer Support</h1>
					<p class="chat-subtitle">
						<span class="status-dot"></span> Live Automated Spec Assistant
					</p>
				</div>
			</div>
			<div class="header-badges">
				<span class="badge">Deterministic Knowledge</span>
				<span class="badge-policy">Regulatory Compliant</span>
			</div>
		</header>

		<!-- Transcript area -->
		<div class="chat-transcript">
			{#each messages as msg (msg.id)}
				<div class="message-row {msg.sender}">
					<div class="message-bubble {msg.isRefusal ? 'refusal' : ''}">
						{#if msg.sender === 'bot' && msg.topicTitle}
							<div class="bubble-tag {msg.isRefusal ? 'tag-refusal' : ''}">
								{msg.topicTitle}
							</div>
						{/if}
						<div class="bubble-text">{msg.text}</div>
						<div class="bubble-meta">{msg.timestamp}</div>
					</div>
				</div>
			{/each}

			{#if isThinking}
				<div class="message-row bot">
					<div class="message-bubble thinking">
						<span class="dot"></span>
						<span class="dot"></span>
						<span class="dot"></span>
					</div>
				</div>
			{/if}
		</div>

		<!-- Quick prompt chips -->
		<div class="quick-prompts-tray">
			<div class="prompts-label">Suggested Test Questions:</div>
			<div class="chips-scroll">
				{#each quickQuestions as q}
					<button type="button" class="chip-btn" onclick={() => handleSend(q)}>
						{q}
					</button>
				{/each}
			</div>
		</div>

		<!-- Input bar -->
		<footer class="chat-input-bar">
			<input
				type="text"
				class="chat-input"
				placeholder="Ask about flavours, ingredients, pricing, or instructions..."
				bind:value={userInput}
				onkeydown={handleKeyDown}
			/>
			<button
				type="button"
				class="send-btn"
				onclick={() => handleSend()}
				disabled={!userInput.trim()}
			>
				Send
			</button>
		</footer>
	</div>

	<div class="spec-sidebar">
		<h2 class="sidebar-title">Chatbot Architecture & Policy</h2>
		<div class="policy-card">
			<h3 class="card-subtitle">Zero AI Hallucination</h3>
			<p class="policy-desc">
				This chatbot operates purely on client-side pattern extraction mapped directly to the locked
				product specification (<code>brand/product-spec.md</code>). It makes no external API calls.
			</p>
		</div>

		<div class="policy-card">
			<h3 class="card-subtitle">Enforced Claim Bans</h3>
			<p class="policy-desc">
				Strict boundary conditions intercept and refuse medical queries or false certification
				inquiries (such as "is it organic?", "gluten-free?", or health claims).
			</p>
		</div>

		<div class="policy-card">
			<h3 class="card-subtitle">Standard Responses</h3>
			<p class="policy-desc">
				Handles damaged pack reports with immediate replacement instructions, quotes locked shelf
				prices ($5.00 NZD / sheet), and explains direct-to-consumer launch availability.
			</p>
		</div>
	</div>
</div>

		max-width: 1120px;
		margin: 2rem auto;
		padding: 0 1.5rem 3rem;
		display: grid;
		grid-template-columns: 1fr 340px;
		gap: 2rem;
		align-items: start;
	}

	.chat-container {
		background: #ffffff;
		border: 1px solid #e1c7f7;
		border-radius: 14px;
		display: flex;
		flex-direction: column;
		height: 720px;
		box-shadow: 0 8px 30px rgba(59, 7, 100, 0.08);
		overflow: hidden;
	}

	.chat-header {
		background: #3b0764;
		color: #ffffff;
		padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem;
		display: flex;
		align-items: center;
		justify-content: space-between;
		border-bottom: 3px solid #e24bff;
	}

	.header-status {
		display: flex;
		align-items: center;
		gap: 1rem;
	}

	.avatar {
		width: 44px;
		height: 44px;
		background: #e24bff;
		color: #3b0764;
		font-weight: 800;
		font-size: 0.95rem;
		border-radius: 50%;
		display: flex;
		align-items: center;
		justify-content: center;
		letter-spacing: -0.02em;
	}

	.chat-title {
		font-size: 1.2rem;
		font-weight: 800;
	}

	.chat-subtitle {
		font-size: 0.8rem;
		opacity: 0.9;
		display: flex;
		align-items: center;
		gap: 0.4rem;
	}

	.status-dot {
		width: 8px;
		height: 8px;
		background: #10b981;
		border-radius: 50%;
		display: inline-block;
	}

	.header-badges {
		display: flex;
		flex-direction: column;
		gap: 0.35rem;
		align-items: flex-end;
	}

	.badge {
		font-size: 0.72rem;
		font-weight: 700;
		background: rgba(226, 75, 255, 0.2);
		border: 1px solid #e24bff;
		color: #fce7fe;
		padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem;
		border-radius: 4px;
	}

	.badge-policy {
		font-size: 0.72rem;
		font-weight: 700;
		background: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.2);
		border: 1px solid #10b981;
		color: #a7f3d0;
		padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem;
		border-radius: 4px;
	}

	.chat-transcript {
		flex: 1;
		overflow-y: auto;
		padding: 1.5rem;
		background: #faf7fd;
		display: flex;
		flex-direction: column;
		gap: 1.25rem;
	}

	.message-row {
		display: flex;
		width: 100%;
	}

	.message-row.user {
		justify-content: flex-end;
	}

	.message-row.bot {
		justify-content: flex-start;
	}

	.message-bubble {
		max-width: 80%;
		padding: 1rem 1.25rem;
		border-radius: 14px;
		position: relative;
		font-size: 0.95rem;
		line-height: 1.5;
	}

	.message-row.user .message-bubble {
		background: #3b0764;
		color: #ffffff;
		border-bottom-right-radius: 2px;
	}

	.message-row.bot .message-bubble {
		background: #ffffff;
		color: #1a1024;
		border: 1px solid #ebd4ff;
		border-bottom-left-radius: 2px;
		box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(59, 7, 100, 0.04);
	}

	.message-bubble.refusal {
		border-left: 4px solid #ef4444;
		background: #fef7f7;
	}

	.bubble-tag {
		font-size: 0.74rem;
		font-weight: 800;
		text-transform: uppercase;
		letter-spacing: 0.04em;
		color: #9333ea;
		margin-bottom: 0.35rem;
	}

	.tag-refusal {
		color: #dc2626 !important;
	}

	.bubble-text {
		white-space: pre-line;
	}

	.bubble-meta {
		font-size: 0.72rem;
		opacity: 0.6;
		margin-top: 0.5rem;
		text-align: right;
	}

	.thinking {
		display: flex;
		align-items: center;
		gap: 0.4rem;
		padding: 0.8rem 1.25rem;
	}

	.dot {
		width: 7px;
		height: 7px;
		background: #9333ea;
		border-radius: 50%;
		animation: pulse 1s infinite alternate;
	}

	.dot:nth-child(2) {
		animation-delay: 0.2s;
	}
	.dot:nth-child(3) {
		animation-delay: 0.4s;
	}

	@keyframes pulse {
		0% {
			opacity: 0.3;
			transform: scale(0.8);
		}
		100% {
			opacity: 1;
			transform: scale(1.1);
		}
	}

	.quick-prompts-tray {
		background: #ffffff;
		border-top: 1px solid #f0deff;
		padding: 0.75rem 1.25rem;

	.chat-input-bar {

		gap: 0.75rem;

	.chat-input {

	.send-btn {

		border: none;
		border-radius: 8px;
		padding: 0 1.5rem;
		font-weight: 700;
		cursor: pointer;
		transition: background 0.15s ease;
	}

	.send-btn:hover:not(:disabled) {
		background: #550a8a;
	}

	.send-btn:disabled {
		opacity: 0.5;

	}

	.spec-sidebar {
		background: #ffffff;

		border-radius: 12px;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate presentation/Stamp-pitch.pptx for INFO123 Video Presentation.

Meets all brief specifications:
- 16:9 widescreen layout
- Slide 1: Title Slide (STAMP, Jacob, INFO123)
- Slide 2: Pitch 1 — Product Innovation & Launch Range (30 seconds)
- Slide 3: Pitch 2 — Market Opportunity & Competitive Advantage (30 seconds)
- Slide 4: Reflection Q1 — Lessons in Prompting, Steering & Fact-Checking (Structured shell)
- Slide 5: Reflection Q2 — Critical Evaluation of AI, Authenticity & Ethics (Structured shell)
"""

from pathlib import Path
import pptx
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT_PPTX = ROOT / "presentation" / "Stamp-pitch.pptx"

# Colors
COLOR_DARK_PURPLE = RGBColor(59, 7, 100)     # #3B0764
COLOR_LIGHT_PURPLE = RGBColor(226, 75, 255)  # #E24BFF
COLOR_TEXT_DARK = RGBColor(26, 16, 36)       # #1A1024
COLOR_TEXT_MUTED = RGBColor(99, 67, 128)     # #634380
COLOR_BG_CARD = RGBColor(251, 247, 255)      # #FBF7FF
COLOR_BORDER = RGBColor(235, 212, 255)       # #EBD4FF
COLOR_WHITE = RGBColor(255, 255, 255)


def add_header(slide, title_text: str, subtitle_text: str, kicker: str = ""):
    header_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.3))
    tf = header_box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    tf.margin_left = tf.margin_top = tf.margin_right = tf.margin_bottom = 0

    if kicker:
        p_kicker = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p_kicker.text = kicker.upper()
        p_kicker.font.size = Pt(11)
        p_kicker.font.bold = True
        p_kicker.font.color.rgb = COLOR_LIGHT_PURPLE
        p_kicker.space_after = Pt(2)
        p_title = tf.add_paragraph()
    else:
        p_title = tf.paragraphs[0]

    p_title.text = title_text
    p_title.font.size = Pt(26)
    p_title.font.bold = True
    p_title.font.color.rgb = COLOR_DARK_PURPLE
    p_title.space_after = Pt(2)

    p_sub = tf.add_paragraph()
    p_sub.text = subtitle_text
    p_sub.font.size = Pt(13)
    p_sub.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT_MUTED


def build_presentation():
    prs = pptx.Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)
    blank_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------
    # SLIDE 1: Title Slide (Dark Purple Background)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------
    slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
    bg1 = slide1.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(7.5)
    )
    bg1.fill.solid()
    bg1.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_DARK_PURPLE
    bg1.line.color.rgb = COLOR_DARK_PURPLE

    # Accent line
    accent = slide1.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(1.2), Inches(1.6), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.08)
    )
    accent.fill.solid()
    accent.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_LIGHT_PURPLE
    accent.line.color.rgb = COLOR_LIGHT_PURPLE

    # Title box
    tb1 = slide1.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1.2), Inches(1.8), Inches(10.5), Inches(4.5))
    tf1 = tb1.text_frame
    tf1.word_wrap = True

    p0 = tf1.paragraphs[0]
    p0.text = "STAMP"
    p0.font.size = Pt(54)
    p0.font.bold = True
    p0.font.color.rgb = COLOR_LIGHT_PURPLE
    p0.space_after = Pt(6)

    p1 = tf1.add_paragraph()
    p1.text = "Peel. Press. Toast."
    p1.font.size = Pt(28)
    p1.font.bold = True
    p1.font.color.rgb = COLOR_WHITE
    p1.space_after = Pt(14)

    p2 = tf1.add_paragraph()
    p2.text = "The Single-Serve Breakfast Spread for Hot Toast"
    p2.font.size = Pt(18)
    p2.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(220, 195, 245)
    p2.space_after = Pt(36)

    p3 = tf1.add_paragraph()
    p3.text = "Presenter: Jacob  |  Course: INFO123 Business AI Project  |  Date: October 2026"
    p3.font.size = Pt(14)
    p3.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(200, 175, 230)

    # Logo on right
    logo_path = ROOT / "brand" / "logo.png"
    if logo_path.exists():
        slide1.shapes.add_picture(str(logo_path), Inches(8.8), Inches(2.3), width=Inches(3.3))

    slide1.notes_slide.notes_text_frame.text = (
        "TITLE SLIDE (0:00–0:10)\n"
        "Welcome. I'm Jacob, and this is Stamp: a New Zealand breakfast spread innovation "
        "designed for hot toast. Over the next minute, I'll walk you through our product "
        "and market opportunity, followed by my personal reflection on building with generative AI."
    )

    # -------------------------------------------------------------
    # SLIDE 2: Pitch 1 — Product Innovation & Launch Range (0:10–0:30)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------
    slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
    add_header(
        slide2,
        "Product Innovation: Peel. Press. Toast.",
        "A single-serve 10 g disc on release film: no knife, no open jar, no morning wash-up.",
        "INVESTOR PITCH — PART 1 (30 SECONDS)"
    )

    # Left Card: How it works & core benefits
    card1 = slide2.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.8), Inches(5.8), Inches(5.1)
    )
    card1.fill.solid()
    card1.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_BG_CARD
    card1.line.color.rgb = COLOR_BORDER

    tb2_left = slide2.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1.1), Inches(2.0), Inches(5.2), Inches(4.7))
    tf2_l = tb2_left.text_frame
    tf2_l.word_wrap = True

    p = tf2_l.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "The Problem & The Gesture"
    p.font.size = Pt(18)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_DARK_PURPLE
    p.space_after = Pt(8)

    points = [
        "Jars Require Infrastructure: Toast eaten away from home (office desks, flats, university halls) demands a knife, an open tub, and a sink to wash up.",
        "The Stamp Solution: A thin 10 g disc of real spread on release film nested in a pocketable card sheet. Peel off, press onto hot toast, and residual heat softens it into an even layer in seconds.",
        "12-Month Pantry Life: Industrial formulation and sealed release film provide 12 months ambient shelf life without refrigeration."
    ]
    for pt in points:
        title, body = pt.split(": ", 1)
        p = tf2_l.add_paragraph()
        p.text = "• " + title + ": "
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.size = Pt(12)
        p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT_DARK
        p.space_after = Pt(6)
        run = p.add_run()
        run.text = body
        run.font.bold = False
        run.font.size = Pt(12)
        run.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT_DARK

    # Right Card: Launch Range & Pack shot
    card2 = slide2.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(6.9), Inches(1.8), Inches(5.6), Inches(5.1)
    )
    card2.fill.solid()
    card2.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_BG_CARD
    card2.line.color.rgb = COLOR_BORDER

    tb2_right = slide2.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(7.2), Inches(2.0), Inches(5.0), Inches(2.2))
    tf2_r = tb2_right.text_frame
    tf2_r.word_wrap = True

    p = tf2_r.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "Four Launch Flavours"
    p.font.size = Pt(18)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_DARK_PURPLE
    p.space_after = Pt(6)

    fl_points = [
        "Salted Butter: Cultured dairy spread (2 g salt / 78 g fat).",
        "Raspberry: Slow-cooked whole fruit paste (150 g fruit / 100 g).",
        "Yeast Extract: Savory umami paste (80% yeast, 15.5% barley malt).",
        "Peanut: 96% roasted peanuts + hard fat anti-separation stabilizer."
    ]
    for fp in fl_points:
        p = tf2_r.add_paragraph()
        p.text = "✔ " + fp
        p.font.size = Pt(11.5)
        p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT_DARK
        p.space_after = Pt(3)

    # Insert pack shot
    pack_path = ROOT / "brand" / "pack.png"
    if pack_path.exists():
        slide2.shapes.add_picture(str(pack_path), Inches(7.5), Inches(4.3), height=Inches(2.3))

    slide2.notes_slide.notes_text_frame.text = (
        "PITCH SLIDE 1 (0:10–0:30)\n"
        "Eating toast away from a kitchen is broken: you have to carry a heavy jar, find a knife, "
        "and wash it in an office or hall sink. Stamp fixes this with a peel-and-press spread disc. "
        "You peel a 10-gram portion off the release film, press it directly onto hot toast, and the "
        "heat melts it into an even layer in seconds. We launch with four distinct flavours: Salted Butter, "
        "Raspberry, Yeast extract, and Peanut—all packaged in an 8-stamp card sheet with a 12-month pantry shelf life."
    )

    # -------------------------------------------------------------
    # SLIDE 3: Pitch 2 — Market Opportunity & Unit Economics (0:30–1:00)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------
    slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
    add_header(
        slide3,
        "Market Opportunity & Competitive Advantage",
        "$341M category with 24% growth, premium tier expansion, and zero portion-format rivals.",
        "INVESTOR PITCH — PART 2 (30 SECONDS)"
    )

    # Left: Economics & Market stats
    card3_left = slide3.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.8), Inches(5.8), Inches(5.1)
    )
    card3_left.fill.solid()
    card3_left.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_BG_CARD
    card3_left.line.color.rgb = COLOR_BORDER

    tb3_left = slide3.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1.1), Inches(2.0), Inches(5.2), Inches(4.7))
    tf3_l = tb3_left.text_frame
    tf3_l.word_wrap = True

    p = tf3_l.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "Verified NZ Breakfast Data"
    p.font.size = Pt(18)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_DARK_PURPLE

    mkt_points = [

        "Unit Economics: Priced at $5.00 NZD per 80 g sheet ($6.25/100g). Above jar medians ($2.15/100g) because buyers pay for portion control and pocket convenience.",

    for pt in mkt_points:
        title, body = pt.split(": ", 1)
        p = tf3_l.add_paragraph()
        p.text = "• " + title + ": "
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.size = Pt(11.5)

        p.space_after = Pt(5)
        run = p.add_run()

    nb4.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(239, 68, 68)
    tf_nb4 = nb4.text_frame
    p_nb4 = tf_nb4.paragraphs[0]

# Stamp Video Presentation — Timing & Script Sheet

**Course:** INFO123 Business AI Project  
**Deliverable:** 2–3 Minute Video Presentation (`.mp4` / `.mov` in Talking-Head format)  
**Strict Requirements:**  
- **Hard stop:** Must conclude before 3m29s (exceeding 3m29s forfeits excellence grades).
- **Pitch limit:** Part 1 (Investor Pitch) must be 1 minute maximum (strict).
- **Format:** Talking-head video (your face visible to camera alongside the slides).
- **AI restriction:** Part 2 (Personal Reflection) must be your own work in your own voice.

---

## Overall Timing Breakdown

| Section | Slide | Target Time | Cumulative | Content |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Intro** | Slide 1 (Title) | 0:00 – 0:08 | 0:08 | Title, name, brief opening |
| **Pitch 1** | Slide 2 (Product) | 0:08 – 0:34 | 0:34 | Problem, peel-and-press format, 4 launch flavours |
| **Pitch 2** | Slide 3 (Market) | 0:34 – 0:58 | 0:58 | $341M market growth, format void, unit economics ($5.00/sheet) |
| **Pitch Wrap** | Transition | 0:58 – 1:00 | 1:00 | Hard pitch cutoff at exactly 60 seconds |
| **Reflection 1** | Slide 4 (AI Lessons) | 1:00 – 1:55 | 1:55 | Prompting, context engineering, verification, pivotal moment |
| **Reflection 2** | Slide 5 (Ethics & Slop) | 1:55 – 2:45 | 2:45 | Combating AI slop, regulatory liability, knowledge worker ethics |
| **Wrap & Sign-off** | Slide 5 / Outro | 2:45 – 2:55 | 2:55 | Conclusion & final thank you (well clear of 3:29 limit) |

---

## Part 1: Investor Pitch Script (0:00 – 1:00)

*Read at a natural, energetic conversational pace (~130–140 words per minute). Word count for this pitch script is 132 words (approx. 52–56 seconds spoken).*

### Slide 1: Title (0:00 – 0:08)
> "Kia ora. I'm Jacob, and this is Stamp: a New Zealand breakfast spread innovation engineered for hot toast."

### Slide 2: Pitch 1 — Product Innovation & Launch Range (0:08 – 0:34)
> "Eating toast away from a full kitchen is broken. When you're in a student hall, flat, or office desk, nobody wants to lug a sticky 750-gram jar, track down a table knife, and wash it in an office sink.
> 
> Stamp reinvents the format with a thin, 10-gram disc of real spread on release film. You peel it off, press it onto hot toast, and residual heat softens it into an even spread in seconds. No knife, no open jar, no morning mess. 
> 
> We launch with four distinct flavours: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, and Peanut—pantry-stable for 12 months in an 8-stamp card sheet."

### Slide 3: Pitch 2 — Market Opportunity & Competitive Advantage (0:34 – 0:58)
> "Our analysis of New Zealand breakfast retail sales shows spreads revenue grew 24% to 341 million dollars, with the premium tier surging 29% to 113 million. Yet across 154 existing spread products, not one offers a single-serve portion format. 
> 
> Supermarket jars like Pic's or Fix & Fogg compete on bulk weight, but they are messy and stationary. At five dollars a sheet—just 63 cents a toast portion—Stamp captures premium convenience. With an assumed manufacturing cost of one-fifty, we retain a strong one-dollar-seventy-five gross margin per sheet. Stamp is ready to own portable breakfast."

*(Transition to reflection at 1:00)*

---

## Part 2: Personal Reflection Guidance (1:00 – 2:45)

*Per the assignment brief, this part MUST be in your own words without AI generation. Use the following structured cue points to guide your speaking.*

### Slide 4: Reflection Question 1 — Working with Generative AI (1:00 – 1:55)
*Target duration: ~55 seconds*

**Key prompts to address:**
1. **Prompting & Context Engineering:**
   - Mention how you structured distinct sessions rather than one massive unmanageable chat.
   - Explain how you used explicit negative constraints (e.g. banning health claims and certification badges) and role personas to get reliable results.
2. **Fact-Checking & Independent Verification:**
   - Mention checking the raw breakfast sales data: spotting prices above $40 and verifying formulas (`price × units ≈ revenue`) rather than blindly trusting initial AI summaries.
   - Mention verifying real shelf prices independently on New World (e.g. Fix & Fogg $11.99, Pic's $7.79) to benchmark Stamp realistically.
3. **Pivotal Moment & What You'd Do Differently:**
   - Share a concrete example where an AI model gave an unrealistic answer (e.g., assuming chilled butter could sit ambiently without dairy-spread reformulations, or generating hallucinated organic claims) and how you corrected it.
   - State what you would do differently next time (e.g., establishing the locked specification earlier).

### Slide 5: Reflection Question 2 — Authenticity, AI Slop & Ethics (1:55 – 2:45)
*Target duration: ~50 seconds*

**Key prompts to address:**
1. **Combating 'AI Slop':**
   - Explain how you actively stripped out generic corporate jargon ("game-changer", "revolutionary breakfast journey") in favour of plain, punchy facts: "Peel. Press. Toast."
   - Contrast real physical packaging constraints (die-cut card, foil release liners) with typical AI fantasy mockups.
2. **Regulatory & Ethical Hazards:**
   - Emphasize the legal hazards of AI in food and beverage: hallucinated health benefits, false "gluten-free" claims (dangerous when Yeast extract contains barley gluten), and allergen responsibility (peanut allergy warnings).
   - How human steering was essential to enforce strict compliance with New Zealand Food Standards.
3. **The Role of the Future Knowledge Worker:**
   - Conclude with your takeaway: Generative AI accelerates drafting, but human judgment, taste, skepticism, and ultimate accountability can never be outsourced to a model.

---

## Recording & Export Instructions

1. **Software:** Open `presentation/Stamp-pitch.pptx` in Microsoft PowerPoint.
2. **Camera Setup:** Go to **Record** > **Record Slide Show** (or **From Beginning**).
   - Ensure your webcam is enabled in the bottom-right or corner of the screen so your talking head is clearly visible alongside the slides.
   - Check lighting (face well lit from the front, no heavy backlighting).
   - Test microphone audio levels.
3. **Execution:**
   - Start the recording and deliver the pitch following the timing marks.
   - Keep an eye on the running timer: Pitch concludes at ~0:58; Reflection concludes around 2:45.
   - Conclude and stop recording before **3:20** (safe buffer before the 3:29 penalty).
4. **Export:**
   - Click **File** > **Export** > **Create a Video** (or **Export As** > **Format: MP4**).
   - Select Full HD (1080p).
   - Save the exported file (e.g. `Jacob-Stamp-Presentation.mp4`).
5. **Verify:**
   - Open the `.mp4` file and watch it through: confirm video plays, audio is crisp and in sync, your face is visible, and duration is between 2:30 and 3:00.

274: 	topicId: 'unknown',
275: 	topicTitle: 'Support Guide',
276: 	answer:
277: 		"I'm here to help with all questions about Stamp! You can ask about:\n\n• What Stamp is and how the peel-and-press system works\n• How to use it on hot toast\n• Our four launch flavours (Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, Peanut)\n• Allergens, nutrition, and ingredient disclosures\n• Pricing ($5.00 NZD per 8-stamp sheet / $6.25 per 100 g)\n• Where to buy and availability\n• Replacements for damaged or crushed sheets\n• How Stamp compares to supermarket jars\n\nWhat would you like to know?"
278: };

280: export function matchQuestion(input: string): BotResponse {
281: 	const text = input.trim();
282: 	if (!text) {
283: 		return FALLBACK_RESPONSE;
284: 	}
285: 
286: 	const lower = text.toLowerCase();
287: 
288: 	// 1. Check high-priority refusals and specific triggers first
289: 	// Medical advice
290: 	if (
291: 		/\b(stomach|tummy|gut|digest|digestive|health|healthy|medical|medicine|cure|treat|remedy|sick|illness|disease|nausea|doctor)\b/i.test(
292: 			lower
293: 		)
294: 	) {
295: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'medical_advice')!;
296: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer, isRefusal: true };
297: 	}
298: 
299: 	// Claim bans (gluten-free, organic, low sugar, etc.)
300: 	if (
301: 		/\b(gluten[-\s]?free|celiac|coeliac|organic|low[-\s]?sugar|sugar[-\s]?free|better for you|diet)\b/i.test(
302: 			lower
303: 		)
304: 	) {
305: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'claim_bans')!;
306: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer, isRefusal: true };
307: 	}
308: 
309: 	// Crushed / damaged
310: 	if (/\b(crushed|damaged|broken|squashed|ruined|torn|melted|complaint)\b/i.test(lower)) {
311: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'crushed_sheet')!;
312: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
313: 	}
314: 
315: 	// Jar comparison
316: 	if (
317: 		/\b(jar|jars|versus|vs|fix & fogg|pics|nutella)\b/i.test(lower) &&
318: 		/\b(compare|comparison|versus|vs|than|why|expensive|different|difference)\b/i.test(lower)
319: 	) {
320: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'jar_comparison')!;
321: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
322: 	}
323: 
324: 	// Nut / peanut / allergen
325: 	if (
326: 		/\b(peanuts?|nuts?|allergen|allergens|allergy|allergic|dairy|milk|lactose)\b/i.test(lower) &&
327: 		!/flavour|flavor|range|varieties/i.test(lower)
328: 	) {
329: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'allergens_peanut')!;
330: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
331: 	}
332: 
333: 	// How to use
334: 	if (
335: 		/how (do i|to|can i) (use|apply|put|eat)/i.test(lower) ||
336: 		/\b(instructions|directions|how does it work)\b/i.test(lower) ||
337: 		(lower.includes('how') && lower.includes('use'))
338: 	) {
339: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'how_to_use')!;
340: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
341: 	}
342: 
343: 	// Price / cost
344: 	if (
345: 		/\b(price|pricing|cost|costs|expensive|nzd|\$|dollars?|cents?)\b/i.test(lower) ||
346: 		/how much/i.test(lower)
347: 	) {
348: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'price')!;
349: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
350: 	}
351: 
352: 	// Where to buy
353: 	if (
354: 		/where (can i|to|do i) (buy|get|purchase|find|order)/i.test(lower) ||
355: 		/\b(supermarket|supermarkets|stockist|stockists|stores?|shops?|retailers?|where to buy)\b/i.test(
356: 			lower
357: 		) ||
358: 		(lower.includes('where') && (lower.includes('buy') || lower.includes('purchase')))
359: 	) {
360: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'where_to_buy')!;
361: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
362: 	}
363: 
364: 	// Flavours
365: 	if (
366: 		/\b(flavours?|flavors?|varieties|tastes?)\b/i.test(lower) ||
367: 		(/what/i.test(lower) && /flavour|flavor/i.test(lower))
368: 	) {
369: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'flavours')!;
370: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
371: 	}
372: 
373: 	// What is a Stamp
374: 	if (
375: 		/what (is|are) (a )?stamp/i.test(lower) ||
376: 		/tell me (about )?stamp/i.test(lower) ||
377: 		/what('s| is) this/i.test(lower) ||
378: 		(lower.includes('what') && lower.includes('stamp'))
379: 	) {
380: 		const topic = TOPICS.find((t) => t.id === 'what_is_stamp')!;
381: 		return { topicId: topic.id, topicTitle: topic.title, answer: topic.answer };
382: 	}
383: 
384: 	// Scoring fallback across remaining topics
385: 	let bestTopic: Topic | null = null;
386: 	let bestScore = 0;
387: 
388: 	for (const topic of TOPICS) {
389: 		let score = 0;
390: 		for (const pat of topic.patterns) {
391: 			if (pat.test(lower)) score += 3;
392: 		}
393: 		for (const kw of topic.keywords) {
394: 			if (lower.includes(kw.toLowerCase())) score += 1;
395: 		}
396: 		if (score > bestScore) {
397: 			bestScore = score;
398: 			bestTopic = topic;
399: 		}
400: 	}
401: 
402: 	if (bestTopic && bestScore >= 2) {
403: 		return {
404: 			topicId: bestTopic.id,
405: 			topicTitle: bestTopic.title,
406: 			answer: bestTopic.answer,
407: 			isRefusal: bestTopic.isRefusal
408: 		};
409: 	}
410: 
411: 	return FALLBACK_RESPONSE;
412: }

35: 		'How does it compare with a jar of peanut butter?'
36: 	];
37: 
38: 	function getTimeString() {
39: 		const now = new Date();
40: 		return now.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
41: 	}
42: 
43: 	function handleSend(textToSend?: string) {
44: 		const query = (textToSend || userInput).trim();
45: 		if (!query) return;
46: 
47: 		// Add user message
48: 		const userMsg: Message = {
49: 			id: Date.now(),
50: 			sender: 'user',
51: 			text: query,
52: 			timestamp: getTimeString()
53: 		};
54: 		messages.push(userMsg);
55: 		userInput = '';
56: 		isThinking = true;
57: 
58: 		// Slight delay for realistic chat feel
59: 		setTimeout(() => {
60: 			const result: BotResponse = matchQuestion(query);
61: 			const botMsg: Message = {
62: 				id: Date.now() + 1,
63: 				sender: 'bot',
64: 				text: result.answer,
65: 				topicTitle: result.topicTitle,
66: 				isRefusal: result.isRefusal,
67: 				timestamp: getTimeString()
68: 			};
69: 			messages.push(botMsg);
70: 			isThinking = false;
71: 		}, 180);
72: 	}
73: 
74: 	function handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
75: 		if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) {
76: 			e.preventDefault();
77: 			handleSend();
78: 		}
79: 	}
80: </script>

1: # Stamp product spec
2: 
3: Locked from your choices in Stage 1. One number is a planning assumption and is marked as such: the manufactured cost that sits under the $5.00 shelf price.
4: 
5: ## What a Stamp is
6: 
7: A Stamp is a 10 g disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. You peel one off and press it onto hot toast. The heat softens it into a layer. No knife and no open jar.
8: 
9: An unopened sheet lives in a pantry for 12 months. The home recipes below are kitchen prototypes, eaten from the fridge within 7 days. Only the industrial formulas are the products we sell, and only those claim the 12-month date.
10: 
11: ## Who it is for
12: 
13: Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion of flavour without carrying a jar or washing a knife.
14: 
15: ## Range and price
16: 
17: | Sheet | Contents | Net weight | Shelf price | Price per 100 g |
18: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
19: | Salted Butter | 8 butter stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
20: | Raspberry | 8 raspberry stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
21: | Yeast extract | 8 yeast-extract stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
22: | Peanut | 8 peanut stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
23: | Mixed | 2 of each flavour | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
24: 
25: $6.25 per 100 g sits above about 90% of branded spread SKUs in the cleaned dataset (90th percentile $5.19 per 100 g). The median branded spread is $2.15 per 100 g. Fix & Fogg's SKUs sit around $2.65 per 100 g. The gap is the portion film and the card, which a jar does not have. The marker is on `data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png`.
26: 
27: ## How to use it
28: 
29: 1. Keep the sheet in a pantry.
30: 2. Peel one stamp off the release film.
31: 3. Press it onto hot toast.
32: 4. Wait a few seconds. The residual heat lays the spread across the slice.
33: 
34: ## Claims we will make
35: 
36: - Peel and press onto hot toast.
37: - One stamp is one portion, 10 g.
38: - Four flavours, sold as single-flavour sheets and a mixed sheet.
39: - No knife and no jar.
40: - Unopened sheet, 12 months in a pantry.
41: 
42: ## Claims we will not make
43: 
44: - Health treatment, "better for you," low-sugar, organic, or gluten-free.
45: - That Salted Butter is a pat of fridge butter. The sold disc is a shelf-stable butter spread. In Australia and New Zealand the word butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard (milkfat, no added oil). The sheet shows the flavour name, then the word spread. The ingredient list names cultured butterfat.
46: - That Yeast extract is Marmite or Vegemite. Those names, jars, and trade dress do not appear on the pack or the site.
47: 
48: ## Allergens
49: 
50: | Flavour | Contains | Also stated on every sheet |
51: | --- | --- | --- |
52: | Salted Butter | Milk | Made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. |
53: | Raspberry | No major allergen in the recipe | Same facility statement. |
54: | Yeast extract | Gluten (barley) | Same facility statement. |
55: | Peanut | Peanuts | Same facility statement. |
56: | Mixed | Milk, gluten, peanuts | Same facility statement. |
57: 
58: ## Home prototypes
59: 
60: Each batch is eight stamps, 80 g. Shape into 10 g discs, press each onto a square of baking paper, and chill until they hold. Eat within 7 days. These batches test flavour and the peel-and-press gesture. They are not the shelf-stable product.
61: 
62: **Salted Butter.** 78 g unsalted butter, softened, beaten with 2 g fine salt.
63: 
64: **Raspberry.** 120 g raspberries, 30 g caster sugar, and 5 g lemon juice, cooked and stirred until 80 g of thick paste remains. Cool before portioning.
65: 
66: **Yeast extract.** 55 g yeast extract, 15 g tomato paste, 8 g black treacle, and 2 g salt, warmed and stirred into a paste that holds a disc. This prototypes the salty yeast flavour. The sold paste is the industrial formula below, not a scooped jar of an existing brand.
67: 
68: **Peanut.** 85 g roasted peanuts and 1.5 g fine salt, ground to a firm paste and portioned before the oil separates.
69: 
70: ## Industrial formulas
71: 
72: Deposit 10 g ± 0.5 g onto release film, cut, nest eight discs in a card sheet, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check or a film that will not release is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. Shelf life is 12 months, ambient, unopened.
73: 
74: **Salted Butter.** Cultured butterfat and salt at the same 2 g salt per 78 g fat as the home batch. Moisture is low enough that the sealed disc stays stable in a pantry and still softens on hot toast. No added oil, so the dairy description stays honest. On the sheet the flavour name is Salted Butter and the word under it is spread.
75: 
76: **Raspberry.** The home ratio (raspberry, sugar, lemon), cooked to the same thick paste and deposited at 10 g. Stability comes from the solids in the cook and the seal, not from a preservative claim. The label says it is made with 150 g of raspberries per 100 g, which is this cook: 120 g of fruit reduced to 80 g.
77: 
78: **Yeast extract.** Our yeast-extract paste, deposited at 10 g: yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, vegetable concentrate 2%. The salt share matches the home batch. Barley malt extract sits above salt, and vegetable concentrate sits below it, so the ingredient list stays in the order above. Contains gluten. The flavour name is Yeast extract. The pack does not say Marmite or Vegemite.
79: 
80: **Peanut.** Roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% as the hard-fat stabiliser, and salt 1.7%, close to the 1.5 g salt in the home batch. The stabiliser keeps the disc from oiling off across 12 months. Contains peanuts.
81: 
82: The nutrition panels on the backs are calculated from these proportions and published composition figures. They are not a laboratory assay.
83: 
84: ## Manufactured cost (assumption)
85: 
86: You chose the $5.00 shelf price. You did not choose a cost target. Until Stage 4 prices a real manufacturer, the spec uses this stack:
87: 
88: | | Per sheet | Per stamp |

1: # Stamp Video Presentation — Timing & Script Sheet

3: **Course:** INFO123 Business AI Project  
4: **Deliverable:** 2–3 Minute Video Presentation (`.mp4` / `.mov` in Talking-Head format)  
5: **Strict Requirements:**

7: - **Pitch limit:** Part 1 (Investor Pitch) must be 1 minute maximum (strict).
8: - **Format:** Talking-head video (your face visible to camera alongside the slides).
9: - **AI restriction:** Part 2 (Personal Reflection) must be your own work in your own voice.
10: 
11: ---
12: 
13: ## Overall Timing Breakdown
14:

16: |---|---|---|---|---|

27: ## Part 1: Investor Pitch Script (0:00 – 1:00)
28: 
29: *Read at a natural, energetic conversational pace (~130–140 words per minute). Word count for this pitch script is 132 words (approx. 52–56 seconds spoken).*
30: 
31: ### Slide 1: Title (0:00 – 0:08)
32: > "Kia ora. I'm Jacob, and this is Stamp: a New Zealand breakfast spread innovation engineered for hot toast."
33: 
34: ### Slide 2: Pitch 1 — Product Innovation & Launch Range (0:08 – 0:34)
35: > "Eating toast away from a full kitchen is broken. When you're in a student hall, flat, or office desk, nobody wants to lug a sticky 750-gram jar, track down a table knife, and wash it in an office sink.
36: > 
37: > Stamp reinvents the format with a thin, 10-gram disc of real spread on release film. You peel it off, press it onto hot toast, and residual heat softens it into an even spread in seconds. No knife, no open jar, no morning mess. 
38: > 
39: > We launch with four distinct flavours: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, and Peanut—pantry-stable for 12 months in an 8-stamp card sheet."
40: 
41: ### Slide 3: Pitch 2 — Market Opportunity & Competitive Advantage (0:34 – 0:58)
42: > "Our analysis of New Zealand breakfast retail sales shows spreads revenue grew 24% to 341 million dollars, with the premium tier surging 29% to 113 million. Yet across 154 existing spread products, not one offers a single-serve portion format. 
43: > 
44: > Supermarket jars like Pic's or Fix & Fogg compete on bulk weight, but they are messy and stationary. At five dollars a sheet—just 63 cents a toast portion—Stamp captures premium convenience. With an assumed manufacturing cost of one-fifty, we retain a strong one-dollar-seventy-five gross margin per sheet. Stamp is ready to own portable breakfast."
45: 
46: *(Transition to reflection at 1:00)*
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## Part 2: Personal Reflection Guidance (1:00 – 2:45)
51: 
52: *Per the assignment brief, this part MUST be in your own words without AI generation. Use the following structured cue points to guide your speaking.*
53: 
54: ### Slide 4: Reflection Question 1 — Working with Generative AI (1:00 – 1:55)
55: *Target duration: ~55 seconds*
56: 
57: **Key prompts to address:**
58: 1. **Prompting & Context Engineering:**
59:    - Mention how you structured distinct sessions rather than one massive unmanageable chat.
60:    - Explain how you used explicit negative constraints (e.g. banning health claims and certification badges) and role personas to get reliable results.
61: 2. **Fact-Checking & Independent Verification:**
62:    - Mention checking the raw breakfast sales data: spotting prices above $40 and verifying formulas (`price × units ≈ revenue`) rather than blindly trusting initial AI summaries.
63:    - Mention verifying real shelf prices independently on New World (e.g. Fix & Fogg $11.99, Pic's $7.79) to benchmark Stamp realistically.
64: 3. **Pivotal Moment & What You'd Do Differently:**
65:    - Share a concrete example where an AI model gave an unrealistic answer (e.g., assuming chilled butter could sit ambiently without dairy-spread reformulations, or generating hallucinated organic claims) and how you corrected it.
66:    - State what you would do differently next time (e.g., establishing the locked specification earlier).
67: 
68: ### Slide 5: Reflection Question 2 — Authenticity, AI Slop & Ethics (1:55 – 2:45)
69: *Target duration: ~50 seconds*
70: 
71: **Key prompts to address:**
72: 1. **Combating 'AI Slop':**
73:    - Explain how you actively stripped out generic corporate jargon ("game-changer", "revolutionary breakfast journey") in favour of plain, punchy facts: "Peel. Press. Toast."
74:    - Contrast real physical packaging constraints (die-cut card, foil release liners) with typical AI fantasy mockups.
75: 2. **Regulatory & Ethical Hazards:**
76:    - Emphasize the legal hazards of AI in food and beverage: hallucinated health benefits, false "gluten-free" claims (dangerous when Yeast extract contains barley gluten), and allergen responsibility (peanut allergy warnings).
77:    - How human steering was essential to enforce strict compliance with New Zealand Food Standards.
78: 3. **The Role of the Future Knowledge Worker:**
79:    - Conclude with your takeaway: Generative AI accelerates drafting, but human judgment, taste, skepticism, and ultimate accountability can never be outsourced to a model.

import { env } from '$env/dynamic/private';

export interface ChatMessage {
	role: 'system' | 'user' | 'assistant';
	content: string;
}

export interface OpenRouterResult {
	success: boolean;
	answer?: string;
	model?: string;
	source: 'openrouter' | 'fallback_deterministic';
	fallbackReason?: string;
	errorDetail?: string;
}

export const STAMP_SYSTEM_PROMPT = `You are the official customer support assistant for STAMP (Stamp Spreads Ltd, Auckland, New Zealand).

Your answers MUST adhere strictly to the locked Stamp product specification and regulatory policies below. You must NEVER hallucinate ingredients, make unverified claims, or contradict the specification.

### 1. WHAT STAMP IS
- Stamp is a peel-and-press spread disc for toast.
- Each stamp is a thin, single-serve 10 g disc of real spread on a food-safe release film, nested flat in a printed card sheet.
- To use: 
  1. Keep the card sheet in the pantry.
  2. Peel one 10 g stamp disc off the release film.
  3. Press it directly onto freshly toasted, hot toast.
  4. Wait a few seconds: residual toast heat softens the spread into an even layer across the slice.
- No knife needed, no open jar to carry, and no morning wash-up.
- Unopened sheets are shelf-stable at room temperature (ambient pantry storage) for 12 months.

### 2. TARGET CUSTOMER & USE CASE
- Designed for anyone eating toast away from a fully equipped kitchen: university halls, student flats, office breakrooms, camping, or commuting with a bag.
- Eliminates the need to carry sticky 750 g jars or wash knives in communal office sinks.

### 3. PRODUCT RANGE & PRICING
- Every Stamp sheet is priced at $5.00 NZD retail.
- Each sheet contains 8 individual 10 g stamps (80 g net weight).
- This equals $6.25 NZD per 100 g (approx. $0.63 NZD per toast portion).
- Available varieties:
  1. Salted Butter (8 stamps, 80 g) - $5.00 NZD
  2. Raspberry (8 stamps, 80 g) - $5.00 NZD
  3. Yeast extract (8 stamps, 80 g) - $5.00 NZD
  4. Peanut (8 stamps, 80 g) - $5.00 NZD
  5. Mixed Sheet (2 stamps of each of the 4 flavours, 80 g) - $5.00 NZD
- Price comparison with supermarket jars: Jars (Pic's at ~$2.05/100g, Fix & Fogg at ~$2.65/100g) are cheaper per 100 g because they are bulk containers meant for kitchen cupboards with a knife and sink. Stamp is priced at $6.25/100g for the engineered release film, single-serve portion control, and pocket convenience.

### 4. EXACT INDUSTRIAL FORMULATIONS & INGREDIENTS
- Salted Butter Spread:
  * Formula: Cultured butterfat and salt (2 g salt to 78 g fat).
  * No added vegetable oils or artificial preservatives.
  * Formulated with low moisture so it is ambient pantry-stable for 12 months, yet melts smoothly onto hot toast.
  * Identity standard: Sold as "Salted Butter Spread", not a pat of fridge butter.
  * Allergen: CONTAINS MILK.
- Raspberry Spread:
  * Formula: Whole raspberries, caster sugar, and fresh lemon juice cooked down to a thick paste.
  * Made with 150 g whole fruit per 100 g finished paste (120 g fruit reduced to 80 g).
  * Naturally preserved via reduction solids and hermetic release seal; no artificial preservatives.
  * Allergen: No major allergens in recipe.
- Yeast extract Spread:
  * Formula: Yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, vegetable concentrate 2%.
  * Deep, savory umami paste.
  * Contains gluten from barley malt extract.
  * Important: Proprietary recipe. NEVER describe or refer to this as Marmite or Vegemite.
  * Allergen: CONTAINS GLUTEN (barley).
- Peanut Spread:
  * Formula: Roasted peanuts 96%, hard vegetable fat 2.3% (anti-separation stabilizer), salt 1.7%.
  * Stabilizer prevents oil from separating or leaking into the card over 12 months.
  * Allergen: CONTAINS PEANUTS.

### 5. MANDATORY ALLERGEN & FACILITY DECLARATIONS
- Salted Butter: Contains Milk.
- Raspberry: No major allergen in recipe.
- Yeast extract: Contains Gluten (barley).
- Peanut: Contains Peanuts.
- Mixed Sheet: Contains Milk, Gluten, and Peanuts.
- Mandatory declaration on EVERY sheet: "Made in a facility that handles milk, gluten, and peanuts."

### 6. STRICT REGULATORY REFUSALS & CLAIM BANS (CRITICAL)
You must strictly refuse or debunk the following queries:
1. NO Medical or Therapeutic Claims:
   - If asked if Stamp cures, treats, relieves, or helps stomach pain, digestion, nausea, gut issues, or any illness:
   - STRICT REFUSAL: Clearly state that Stamp is a food spread for toast, not a medical or therapeutic treatment. Stamp makes no therapeutic claims and does not prevent, treat, or cure any condition. Strongly advise consulting a qualified medical professional.
2. NO Unbacked Dietary or Certification Claims:
   - Stamp NEVER makes claims to be "organic", "gluten-free", "low-sugar", "sugar-free", "keto", or "better for you".
   - If asked if Stamp is gluten-free: Explicitly state that Stamp is NOT gluten-free. Yeast extract contains gluten from barley malt (15.5%), and all sheets are packed in a facility handling gluten, milk, and peanuts.
   - If asked if Stamp is organic: State clearly that Stamp does not claim to be organic and does not carry unverified certification badges.
3. NO Brand Encroachment:
   - Never say Salted Butter is cold table butter.
   - Never claim Yeast extract is Marmite or Vegemite.

### 7. CUSTOMER SERVICE POLICIES
- Damaged, crushed, or melted sheets:
  * Sincerely apologize.
  * Tell the customer to take a quick photo of the damaged card sheet showing the batch number printed on the back, and email support@stampbreakfast.nz.
  * Stamp will immediately dispatch a fresh replacement sheet free of charge or issue a full refund.
- Where to buy:
  * Stamp is currently launching direct-to-consumer online via https://stampbreakfast.nz during our initial trial production run.
  * Stamp is not currently stocked in physical supermarkets (such as New World, Countdown/Woolworths, or Pak'nSave).

### 8. TONE & STYLE
- Tone: Concise, friendly, knowledgeable, matter-of-fact New Zealand tone (kiwi-friendly, respectful).
- No corporate AI slop or hyperbolic buzzwords (avoid "game-changer", "revolutionary breakfast journey", "delve", etc.).
- Plain facts, transparent declarations, and direct answers. Keep responses focused and readable (typically 2-4 sentences unless detailed specs are requested).`;

export function getOpenRouterConfig(): { apiKey: string | undefined; model: string } {
	const apiKey =
		env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY ||
		(typeof process !== 'undefined' ? process.env?.OPENROUTER_API_KEY : undefined) ||
		'';
	const model =
		env.OPENROUTER_MODEL ||
		(typeof process !== 'undefined' ? process.env?.OPENROUTER_MODEL : undefined) ||
		'openai/gpt-4o-mini';

	return {
		apiKey: apiKey.trim() || undefined,
		model: model.trim() || 'openai/gpt-4o-mini'
	};
}

export async function askOpenRouter(
	userPrompt: string,
	conversationHistory: ChatMessage[] = []
): Promise<OpenRouterResult> {
	const { apiKey, model } = getOpenRouterConfig();

	if (!apiKey) {
		return {
			success: false,
			source: 'fallback_deterministic',
			fallbackReason: 'NO_API_KEY',
			model
		};
	}

	const messages: ChatMessage[] = [
		{ role: 'system', content: STAMP_SYSTEM_PROMPT },
		...conversationHistory.slice(-8), // Keep last 8 turns for context
		{ role: 'user', content: userPrompt }
	];

	try {
		const controller = new AbortController();
		const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 12000); // 12-second timeout

		const response = await fetch('https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions', {
			method: 'POST',
			headers: {
				Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
				'Content-Type': 'application/json',
				'HTTP-Referer': 'https://stampbreakfast.nz',
				'X-Title': 'Stamp Toast Spreads'
			},
			body: JSON.stringify({
				model,
				messages,
				temperature: 0.2, // Low temperature for high factual adherence
				max_tokens: 500
			}),
			signal: controller.signal
		});

		clearTimeout(timeoutId);

		if (!response.ok) {
			const errorText = await response.text();
			console.warn(`OpenRouter API error (status ${response.status}):`, errorText);
			return {
				success: false,
				source: 'fallback_deterministic',
				fallbackReason: `HTTP_${response.status}`,
				errorDetail: errorText.slice(0, 300),
				model
			};
		}

		const data = await response.json();
		const content = data.choices?.[0]?.message?.content;

		if (!content || typeof content !== 'string') {
			return {
				success: false,
				source: 'fallback_deterministic',
				fallbackReason: 'EMPTY_COMPLETION',
				model
			};
		}

		return {
			success: true,
			answer: content.trim(),
			source: 'openrouter',
			model
		};
	} catch (err: unknown) {
		const errorMsg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
		console.warn('OpenRouter request failed:', errorMsg);
		return {
			success: false,
			source: 'fallback_deterministic',
			fallbackReason: 'NETWORK_EXCEPTION',
			errorDetail: errorMsg,
			model
		};
	}
}

import { json } from '@sveltejs/kit';
import type { RequestHandler } from './$types';
import { askOpenRouter, getOpenRouterConfig, type ChatMessage } from '$lib/server/openrouter';
import { matchQuestion } from '$lib/knowledge';

export const GET: RequestHandler = async () => {
	const config = getOpenRouterConfig();
	return json({
		status: 'ok',
		openrouterConfigured: !!config.apiKey,
		model: config.model,
		fallbackAvailable: true
	});
};

export const POST: RequestHandler = async ({ request }) => {
	try {
		const body = await request.json();
		const message = typeof body?.message === 'string' ? body.message.trim() : '';
		const rawHistory = Array.isArray(body?.history) ? body.history : [];

		if (!message) {
			return json({ error: 'Message is required and cannot be empty.' }, { status: 400 });
		}

		// Filter and sanitize chat history
		const history: ChatMessage[] = rawHistory
			.filter(
				(item: unknown): item is { role: string; content: string } =>
					typeof item === 'object' &&
					item !== null &&
					'role' in item &&
					'content' in item &&
					typeof (item as { role: unknown }).role === 'string' &&
					typeof (item as { content: unknown }).content === 'string'
			)
			.map((item) => ({
				role: (['user', 'assistant', 'system'].includes(item.role)
					? item.role
					: 'user') as ChatMessage['role'],
				content: item.content.slice(0, 1000)
			}));

		// 1. Attempt OpenRouter AI completion
		const openRouterRes = await askOpenRouter(message, history);

		if (openRouterRes.success && openRouterRes.answer) {
			// Check if LLM output reflects a refusal response
			const lowerAns = openRouterRes.answer.toLowerCase();
			const isRefusal =
				lowerAns.includes('not a medical') ||
				lowerAns.includes('do not provide health advice') ||
				lowerAns.includes('does not make organic') ||
				lowerAns.includes('not gluten-free');

			return json({
				answer: openRouterRes.answer,
				source: 'openrouter',
				model: openRouterRes.model,
				isRefusal,
				timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
			});
		}

		// 2. Fallback cleanly to our deterministic locked spec engine
		const deterministic = matchQuestion(message);

		return json({
			answer: deterministic.answer,
			source: 'fallback_deterministic',
			topicTitle: deterministic.topicTitle,
			isRefusal: deterministic.isRefusal,
			fallbackReason: openRouterRes.fallbackReason || 'DETERMINISTIC_FALLBACK',
			model: openRouterRes.model,
			timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
		});
	} catch (err: unknown) {
		const errorMsg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
		console.error('Chat endpoint error:', errorMsg);

		// Even on JSON parse or unexpected error, serve fallback
		return json(
			{
				answer:
					"I encountered a temporary processing issue. Here is Stamp's standard guide: Stamp is a 10 g peel-and-press toast spread ($5.00 NZD / sheet of 8). Available in Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, and Peanut. For support questions email support@stampbreakfast.nz.",
				source: 'fallback_deterministic',
				topicTitle: 'Error Fallback',
				error: errorMsg
			},
			{ status: 200 }
		);
	}
};
